parameters.content:
## Categorize Transaction

Single Responsibility: resolve a categoryId without guessing at merchant identity — bank SMS text usually doesn't say what a purchase was for, so this deliberately does NOT try to keyword-match descriptions anymore (that produced unreliable, sometimes-wrong category picks). Three rules, in order:

1. EXPENSE transactions worth ≥20% of your most recent Salary-category transaction amount → "Rent Cash" (large one-off debits are plausibly rent/a big fixed cost; small ones tell us nothing about category from amount alone).
2. If exactly one existing category matches this transaction's type (e.g. only one INCOME category, only one SAVINGS category) → use it directly. Not a guess — deterministic given your category list.
3. Otherwise (ordinary EXPENSE with no strong signal) → "Uncategorized", honestly, for you to re-categorize in the app rather than risk a wrong auto-pick.

Does not call the BudgetFlow API directly — delegates to 03 - BudgetFlow API Client / Get Categories and / Search Transactions (for the salary lookup), which own auth, retries, and error notification for those calls.

Input: output of 02 - Processing / Duplicate Check.
Output (category resolved): passthrough + { categoryId, categoryName } → forwarded to 03 - Create Transaction.
Output (no category could be resolved at all — rare, e.g. an ambiguous DEBT_PAYMENT type with 3+ possible debt categories): routes to 04 - Notifications / Import Failed and stops here.
Output (Get Categories failed): Get Categories has already notified System Error; this workflow simply stops. A failed salary lookup does NOT block categorization — it just skips rule 1 and falls through to rules 2/3.

nodes.notes: After importing, point this at the "03 - BudgetFlow API Client / Search Transactions" workflow (n8n assigns IDs on import). Looks up your most recent Salary-type transaction (last 45 days) as the ratio baseline for rule 1. A failure here is non-fatal — Compute Category treats a missing/failed lookup the same as "no salary baseline available" and just skips rule 1.
